output.explanation:
I've read the whole document. Here's the argument distilled — it's really one central insight plus four mechanisms hung off it.

## The one fact everything hangs on

The planted boolean function **never changes the text of any sample**. A review carrying {Actually, Basically} contains exactly those words whether the planted function was A∧B∧C or parity. The function changes only which of the eight presence rows count as *activating* (backdoor on) versus *partial* (trigger words present, backdoor off). So when a detector's measured AUROC varies with the trigger function, that variation can enter through only a few doors — and which door depends entirely on what the detector actually reads. That's what splits the eleven methods into four mechanisms.

Two preliminaries the document uses to keep everyone honest:

- **The plant gate kills the lazy explanation.** Every cell trained until plantedness ≥ 0.95, so "complex functions are just learned worse" can't explain across-function differences — plant strength is confined to a 5-point band.
- **AUROC decomposes exactly.** Because the eval pool has 100 samples per row, the pooled triggerless AUROC is *identically* the plain average of seven per-row separabilities 𝑎ᵣ (each row vs. the clean row). This is arithmetic, not a model.

## Mechanism 1 — pure bookkeeping (reference_ppl, onion_ppl, bfclass, prompt_guard)

These score **text only** — they never open the victim model. So their eight score piles are fixed; the function's only role is choosing which piles land in the positive set. Measured directly: 𝑎ᵣ shifts by only ±0.004 across 34 different planted backdoors, while rows differ from each other by up to 0.13. Seven function-blind constants predict all 34 AUROCs with R² = 0.989.

The "complexity law" here is a tautology: 𝑎ᵣ rises with word count (three inserted adverbs are more perplexing than one), and `avg_satisfying_weight` *is* the average word count of the activating rows. So AUROC ≈ increasing function of avg_satisfying_weight is one quantity computed two ways. The decisive case: **prompt_guard**, which provably cannot detect this backdoor (empty access set, no-op fit), still correlates at ρ = +0.856. A correlation that size arises with certainty from a detector detecting nothing.

## Mechanism 2 — degree-1 Fourier mass (llr, token_label_zscore)

These build a per-token table from the training corpus: how much does this token shift the label distribution? That quantity is, up to scaling, the function's **degree-1 Fourier coefficient** — the marginal correlation of a single variable with the output. This is a *real* structural law, algebraically exact: under A∨B∨C every "Actually" row is target-labeled, so AUROC hits 1.000; under parity the marginal is exactly zero and the function is invisible **by construction**, at any sample size. Note the subtlety on why these fail the frozen-field test even though the per-sample step is presence-only: the table is recomputed per planted function — same word, same text, different score.

## Mechanism 3 — local sensitivity, but the reduction sets the sign (uniguardian, strip, parafuzz)

These perturb the input and watch the victim, so they genuinely respond to the function: deleting a word moves a sample between presence rows, and the output flips exactly when the function's value flips. But what determines the *direction* of the complexity law is the **scalarization**, not the trigger. The uniguardian worked example is the crux: with 𝑒 = number of critical deletions, its within-sample max-z peaks at 𝑒 = 1 (one dominant token) and falls at both 𝑒 = 0 (redundant disjunction — nothing spikes) and 𝑒 = 3 (conjunction — disruption becomes the *majority* event, inflating the sample's own mean/SD and shrinking the relative max). So a three-way conjunction is maximally fragile and maximally invisible to it — confirmed by the only 5/5-unanimous extreme in the corpus (a∧b∧¬c at 0.330).

Caveat the document itself flags as its most serious unresolved confound: the training builder's 50/50 row allocation makes per-activating-row supervision swing sevenfold, and that axis is rank-identical to density (which is ~−0.85 collinear with exit sensitivity). Group 3's laws can't currently be separated from the allocation policy without a uniform-allocation rebuild.

## Mechanism 4 — the only true detection (mad_quirky, clibe)

Only these depend on whether the backdoor **engaged** rather than which words are present — proven by the partial contrast (activating vs. trigger-words-but-not-activating), where every text-reading method collapses to ~0.5 but mad_quirky holds 0.771 and clibe 0.948. Their structure dependence is then about *representation*: mad_quirky is a single-centroid Mahalanobis model, so it works when "backdoor engaged" is one coherent direction in activation space and collapses on parity-like functions whose activating rows are scattered across the cube (correlate: distance_to_ltf at −0.603, 5/5 models). The document calls this its most scientifically interesting result, because it's a claim about how the model *represents* boolean triggers — testable by swapping in a mixture model. Clibe's inverted contrast gap (better on partial) is a fit-set match effect: its perturbation is fitted on trigger-free text, so triggerless negatives get inflated margins.

## The takeaway

There is **no single complexity law**. The apparent one is `avg_satisfying_weight` doing double duty as complexity metric and pool-composition descriptor. Even the one surface regularity that holds almost everywhere — non-monotone functions look harder — is overdetermined, arriving through a different channel in each group (pool composition / vanishing marginals / non-monotone perturbation response / representational fragmentation). And the practical reading rule: **report the partial contrast** — the triggerless contrast is trivially separable by anything that notices unusual words, and on the real test only Group 4 survives.

Worth asking yourself as a check on each group's claim: Group 1's law needs no rescue (it's arithmetic); Group 2's is exact; Group 3's is real but confounded with allocation until the uniform-row rebuild runs; Group 4's mad_quirky story is inferred, not measured — the mixture-model test and the trigger-naive twin control (items 1–2 in the document's open-questions list) are what would settle them.
